traceability.evidence:
Implementation and rule presence: - Rule files exist: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - Both rules are registered in the plugin via src/index.ts: - const RULE_NAMES = ["require-story-annotation", "require-req-annotation", ...]; - rules[name] = mod.default ?? mod; // dynamically loads ./rules/
Core functionality and shared function detection (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED): - Shared detection configuration: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts: - export const DEFAULT_SCOPE: string[] = [ "FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction", ]; - export const EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES = ["all", "exported", "non-exported"]; - Shared scope/export logic: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: - function shouldProcessNode(node: any, scope: string[], exportPriority: string = "all"): boolean { if (!scope.includes(node.type)) return false; const exported = isExportedNode(node); if (exportPriority === "exported" && !exported) return false; if (exportPriority === "non-exported" && exported) return false; return true; } - isExportedNode walks the parent chain for ExportNamedDeclaration / ExportDefaultDeclaration. - require-story-annotation uses shared detection: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts: - Imports DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode from ./helpers/require-story-helpers. - meta.schema enforces: - scope: array, items enum: DEFAULT_SCOPE, uniqueItems: true. - exportPriority: string, enum: EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES. - create(context): - const scope = opts.scope || DEFAULT_SCOPE; - const exportPriority = opts.exportPriority || "all"; - const should = (node: any) => shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority); - returns buildVisitors(context, sourceCode, { shouldProcessNode: should, scope, exportPriority }). - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts builds visitors for: - FunctionDeclaration - FunctionExpression - MethodDefinition - TSDeclareFunction - TSMethodSignature - ArrowFunctionExpression and calls helperReportMissing/helperReportMethod when options.shouldProcessNode(node) is true. - require-req-annotation uses the same detection and scope/export logic: - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts: - Imports DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode from ./helpers/require-story-helpers. - meta.schema mirrors require-story-annotation (scope array with enum: DEFAULT_SCOPE, exportPriority enum: EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES). - create(context): - const rawScope = options?.scope; - const scope = Array.isArray(rawScope) && rawScope.length > 0 ? rawScope : DEFAULT_SCOPE; - const exportPriority = options?.exportPriority ?? "all"; - const shouldCheck = (node: any): boolean => shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority); - runCheck(node) calls checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix: false }) only if shouldCheck(node). - Visitors for: - FunctionDeclaration - FunctionExpression (skips when parent.type === "MethodDefinition") - MethodDefinition - TSDeclareFunction - TSMethodSignature - Tests confirm both rules apply over the same function-like constructs and respect scope/exportPriority: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: - Valid TS cases for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature with @story. - Invalid TS cases when @story is missing for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature. - "require-story-annotation with exportPriority option" verifies exported vs non-exported behavior. - "require-story-annotation with scope option" verifies that only FunctionDeclaration is checked when scope is ["FunctionDeclaration"]. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts: - Valid and invalid cases for FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. - Explicit tests with names like: - "[REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION][Story 003.0] missing @req on FunctionExpression assigned to variable". - TS variants with withTsLanguageOptions. - Scope option tests (scope: ["FunctionDeclaration"]). - exportPriority tests for "exported", "non-exported" across functions and methods.
Arrow functions excluded by default from traceability (part of REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION): - DEFAULT_SCOPE (src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts) does NOT include "ArrowFunctionExpression". - require-story-annotation: - There is a dedicated ArrowFunctionExpression visitor in require-story-visitors.ts, but it only runs when options.shouldProcessNode(node) is true. - With the default scope, shouldProcessNode returns false for ArrowFunctionExpression, so arrows are not enforced by default. - meta.schema for scope only allows entries from DEFAULT_SCOPE, so users cannot add ArrowFunctionExpression via configuration; this keeps the story’s default exclusion intact. - require-req-annotation: - No ArrowFunctionExpression visitor is defined; the rule never enforces @req on arrows. - Tests reflect this behavior: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts includes a valid case: - name: "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED] unannotated arrow function allowed by default", code: `const arrowFn = () => {};`, confirming arrows are not reported.
Common JSDoc/comment parsing strategy (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING): - For @story (require-story-annotation): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: - jsdocHasStory(sourceCode, node): - Uses sourceCode.getJSDocComment(node) and checks jsdoc.value.includes("@story"). - commentsBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node): - Uses sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node) and scans for "@story". - leadingCommentsHasStory(node): - Scans node.leadingComments for "@story". - hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node): - Combines jsdocHasStory, commentsBeforeHasStory, leadingCommentsHasStory, and IO-based helpers from src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts: - linesBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node, LOOKBACK_LINES) - parentChainHasStory(sourceCode, node) - fallbackTextBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node) - Wrapped in try/catch to avoid throwing on malformed JSDoc/AST (graceful error handling). - For @req (require-req-annotation): - src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts provides parallel helpers: - commentContainsReq, linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq. - Uses shared constants LOOKBACK_LINES and FALLBACK_WINDOW from src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts. - All helpers wrapped with guards and try/catch to avoid crashes (e.g., malformed ranges or missing loc). - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts: - getJsdocComment(sourceCode, node) -> sourceCode.getJSDocComment(node). - getLeadingComments(node) and getCommentsBefore(sourceCode, node) to collect all relevant comments. - combineComments(leading, before) merges arrays. - checkReqAnnotation(context, node, options?): - Builds jsdoc + all comments, calls hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, all, context, node). - If !hasReq, calls reportMissing(context, node, enableFix). - reportMissing(context, node, enableFix) uses getNodeName (src/rules/helpers/require-story-utils.ts) to derive a stable name, picks a nameNode (id/key), reports messageId: "missingReq" with data { name, functionName: name }, and conditionally attaches a fix via createMissingReqFix. - This shows both rules use a robust, multi-source comment parsing strategy, tailored respectively to @story and @req, fulfilling REQ-JSDOC-PARSING and REQ-ERROR-HANDLING.
Configurable scope and export priority (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY): - Shared logic: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts::shouldProcessNode implements scope/exportPriority semantics once, used by both rules. - require-story-annotation: - meta.schema enforces the options: - scope: array (enum: DEFAULT_SCOPE, uniqueItems: true). - exportPriority: string (enum: ["all", "exported", "non-exported"]). - create(context) applies defaults when options not provided. - Tests: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: - "require-story-annotation with exportPriority option": * Valid: unexported local() without @story when exportPriority: "exported". * Invalid: exportedMissing() reported when exportPriority: "exported". - "require-story-annotation with scope option": * Valid: arrow function allowed when scope: ["FunctionDeclaration"]. * Invalid: onlyDecl() reported when scope includes FunctionDeclaration. - require-req-annotation: - meta.schema mirrors the same options and enums. - create(context) applies defaults similarly and uses shouldProcessNode. - Tests: - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts contains multiple cases labeled [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE] and [REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY] that verify: - scope filtering (only FunctionDeclaration enforced when scope: ["FunctionDeclaration"]). - exportPriority behavior across exported/non-exported functions, methods, and function expressions.
Error location and user-facing messages (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION, User Experience): - require-story-annotation: - meta.messages.missingStory: - "Function '{{name}}' must have an explicit @story annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @story that points to the implementing story file (for example, docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md)." - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts::reportMissing/context.report({ ... }): - nameNode selected as node.id Identifier, else node.key Identifier, else node; this ensures error is anchored at function name or closest equivalent. - data includes { name, functionName: name } to satisfy error-reporting stories. - fix + suggest insert the shared ANNOTATION (/** @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md */) before the correct target node. - reportMethod similarly anchors on the method name node and includes specific functionName data. - require-req-annotation: - meta.messages.missingReq: - "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @req (for example, '@req REQ-EXAMPLE') referencing the appropriate requirement from the story file." - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts::reportMissing(context, node, enableFix): - Uses getNodeName(node or node.parent) to derive name. - Chooses nameNode as node.id Identifier or node.key Identifier, else node. - context.report with messageId: "missingReq" and data: { name, functionName: name }. - Optional autofix via createMissingReqFix when enableFix is true. - Tests assert correct data and messaging: - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts invalid entries expect: - errors: [{ messageId: "missingReq", data: { name: "baz", functionName: "baz" } }], etc., confirming precise location and contextual naming. - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts invalid entries assert messageId: "missingStory" and expected suggestion text, verifying clarity and actionability.
TypeScript support (REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT): - Implementation: - require-story-annotation: visitors for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature that call helperReportMissing with appropriate targets (including interface parent for TSMethodSignature). - require-req-annotation: visitors for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature, wired to runCheck(node) and thus to checkReqAnnotation. - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts and src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts are written to use node.loc, node.range, and ESLint's sourceCode APIs, enabling TS-specific handling. - Test infrastructure: - tests/utils/ts-language-options.ts: - Exports tsRuleTesterLanguageOptions using @typescript-eslint/parser and ES2022/module parserOptions. - Exports withTsLanguageOptions helper to attach TS languageOptions to RuleTester test cases. - tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts: - Declares @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT in the header. - Defines runAnnotationCheckerTests helper and a rule that calls checkReqAnnotation for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature. - Tests valid/invalid TS cases and autofix behavior for missing @req. - Rule-level tests: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: - Uses withTsLanguageOptions to test TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature with and without @story. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts: - Uses runAnnotationCheckerTests("require-req-annotation", { ... }) to specifically exercise TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature behavior within the rule.

traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md are satisfied. The two required rules, `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation`, are implemented, share a common and configurable function-detection scope (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature) and exportPriority semantics, and exclude arrow functions by default. Both rely on robust, shared parsing strategies for JSDoc and nearby comments, have clear, actionable error messages that report at the function name or closest equivalent, and include defensive error handling around malformed JSDoc or AST structures. TypeScript-specific constructs (TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature) are fully supported and comprehensively tested via shared TS RuleTester configuration and helper utilities. Documentation for both rules exists and matches the implemented behavior and configuration options, with JS and TS examples. Comprehensive Jest/RuleTester tests for these rules, their helpers, and the annotation-checker pass. On this basis, the story is fully implemented and marked as PASSED.
